title: Guarder: A Stable and Lightweight Reconfigurable RRAM-based PIM Accelerator for DNN IP Protection
problem: RRAM-based processing-in-memory accelerators suffer from imprecise weights due to programming stochasticity, limiting model accuracy, and cannot effectively utilize conventional weight encryption/decryption IP protection schemes.
method: Guarder proposes a software-hardware co-design: (1) Hardware: 3T2R cells for reliable MAC operations and reconfigurable inverter operating voltages to encode encryption keys directly in RRAM, (2) Software: Contrastive training ensures high accuracy on authorized chips and degraded performance on unauthorized ones.

title: ADVISOR: Approximate Computing-frienDly High-LeVel Synthesis DesIgn Space ExplORer
problem: High-level synthesis (HLS) enables rapid exploration of hardware implementations, but when combined with approximate computing trade-offs, each design variant must be fully approximated to evaluate area/power vs. accuracy trade-offs, resulting in prohibitively long exploration time.
method: ADVISOR accelerates HLS design space exploration via a static Approximation Friendliness Index (AFI) metric that quickly scores each design for its amenability to approximation. Only designs with high AFI are fully approximated; this filters the design space without expensive full approximation on all variants, achieving 68x speedup over exhaustive exploration.

title: RUPlace: Optimizing Routability via Unified Placement and Routing Formulation
problem: Placement optimization in advanced VLSI designs struggles with routing congestion management; existing methods lack theoretical foundations and decouple placement from routing, missing optimization synergies.
method: ADMM-based placer that alternately optimizes global routing and incremental placement using Wasserstein distance and bilevel optimization. A convex programming model determines optimal cell inflation ratios for global placement while directly minimizing routed congestion.

title: Re4PUF: A Reliable, Reconfigurable ReRAM-based PUF Resilient to DNN and Side Channel Attacks
problem: ReRAM-based Physical Unclonable Functions suffer from unreliability due to read noise and temperature variations, and are vulnerable to Deep Neural Network modeling attacks and Side Channel Attacks.
method: Re4PUF proposes a 3T2R ReRAM-based reconfigurable PUF with digital voltage division cells to improve reliability against read noise and temperature. Adjustable analog inverter supply voltages enable low-cost reconfigurability without ReRAM reprogramming, mitigating DNN and side channel vulnerabilities.

title: 7.2: A 2.2pJ/b 212.5Gb/s PAM-4 Transceiver with >46dB Reach in 5nm FinFET
problem: 100G/lane Ethernet is transitioning to 200G/lane (224Gb/s) to enable 1.6Tb/s infrastructure, requiring power-efficient, long-reach SerDes transceivers that handle signal integrity challenges from cables, connectors, and packages.
method: Long-reach PAM-4 SerDes transceiver in 5nm FinFET with optimized analog front-end for signal compensation; achieves 212.5Gb/s operation with >46dB channel loss compensation and analog power of 2.2pJ/b.

title: A Data-Centric Hardware Accelerator for Efficient Adaptive Radix Tree
problem: Adaptive Radix Tree (ART) operations suffer from redundant tree traversals and high synchronization costs during concurrent read/write operations in databases and key-value stores.
method: Proposes DCART, a data-centric hardware accelerator that exploits temporal and spatial similarities in workloads; coalesces operations targeting the same ART nodes and adaptively caches frequently traversed nodes and their search results.

title: ASDR: Exploiting Adaptive Sampling and Data Reuse for CIM-based Instant Neural Rendering
problem: Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) inference exhibits irregular memory access patterns and high computational overhead, making it unsuitable for low-latency, power-efficient deployment on edge devices. Standard compute architectures cannot bridge the gap between NeRF's memory-bound irregular accesses and the immediacy/power requirements of practical neural rendering.
method: ASDR maps NeRF inference onto computing-in-memory (CIM) arrays to address the memory access bottleneck by performing computation near data storage, eliminating costly DRAM transfers. Adaptive sampling reduces the number of points sampled per ray dynamically based on scene complexity, cutting redundant computation. Data reuse strategies exploit spatial and temporal coherence across adjacent rays and frames to avoid redundant CIM macro activations. Together, these techniques reduce both the number of operations and the energy per operation on the CIM substrate.

title: GoPTX: Fine-grained GPU Kernel Fusion by PTX-level Instruction Flow Weaving
problem: Concurrent kernel execution on GPUs misses opportunities to mitigate warp stalls and improve instruction-level parallelism (ILP) through inter-kernel resource sharing due to sequential default execution of kernels.
method: GoPTX performs fine-grained kernel fusion at the PTX (Parallel Thread Execution) instruction level by establishing a merged control flow graph, interleaving instructions from multiple kernels to minimize pipeline stalls on data hazards; proposes latency-aware instruction weaving algorithm and adaptive code slicing to enlarge scheduling space.

title: Harnessing Conventional Video Processing Insights for Emerging 3D Video Generation Models: A Comprehensive Attention-aware Way
problem: 3D video generation models with full attention mechanisms incur >75% of compute in attention operations, causing high inference latency and energy consumption.
method: Proposes SimPicker, a co-design combining algorithm and hardware: (1) speculation-based similarity exploitation at frame level (coarse) and token level (fine); (2) buffered lookup-table multiplier for FP-INT operations; (3) adaptive grouping strategy to handle workload imbalance from randomly distributed similar tokens.

title: Let-Me-In: (Still) Employing In-pointer Bounds Metadata for Fine-grained GPU Memory Safety
problem: GPU programs written in C/C++ inherit memory safety vulnerabilities such as out-of-bounds accesses. The heterogeneous GPU memory hierarchy (heap, local memory, thousands of concurrent threads) makes it difficult to enforce fine-grained bounds checking with low overhead.
method: LMI aligns GPU memory allocations to powers-of-two boundaries and performs static analysis at compile time to identify and mark pointer arithmetic instructions. Bounds metadata (base and size) is encoded into the unused upper bits of 64-bit GPU virtual address pointers, eliminating separate metadata memory structures. Hardware bounds-checking logic validates each memory access against the in-pointer metadata before issuing the request, adding minimal per-access latency even under thousands of concurrent threads.

title: Power-Constrained Printed Neuromorphic Hardware Training
problem: Printed neuromorphic circuits (pNCs) must operate under severe power budgets from printed batteries or energy harvesters while maintaining task accuracy; traditional penalty-based optimization requires hundreds of training runs to explore power-accuracy tradeoffs.
method: Augmented Lagrangian optimization enforces task-specific power constraints directly during training, computing optimal power-accuracy tradeoffs in a single run. Tested across 13 benchmarks with different activation functions (p-tanh, p-Clipped_ReLU).

title: LVM-MO: A Large Vision Model Pioneer on Full-Chip Mask Optimization
problem: Full-chip mask optimization (MO) challenges in post-Moore era require handling entire layouts with optical proximity and process bias effects; existing clip-level restoration approaches exhibit limited correction, poor generalization, and inefficiency at full-chip scale.
method: Proposes data-driven large vision model (foundation model) for full-chip mask optimization with a layout feature extractor aware of polygon mutual influence in long-range pattern perception, optical physics, and lithography chemistry; treats MO as a vision task enabling learning across diverse mask patterns.

title: Dynamic Partial Deadlock Detection and Recovery via Garbage Collection
problem: Concurrent message-passing programs in Go are susceptible to partial deadlocks where goroutines block indefinitely on channels, causing severe memory leaks in long-running systems. Existing techniques cannot both detect and automatically recover from these partial deadlocks at runtime.
method: GOLF extends Go's garbage collector marking phase to soundly approximate goroutine liveness: a goroutine is considered live only if its channel references are reachable from the GC root set. During GC marking, goroutines blocked on channels with no live senders are flagged as deadlocked. Detected deadlocked goroutines are then automatically cancelled or cleaned up to free memory and restore system progress. The detection integrates directly into the existing GC pause with minimal overhead.

title: Invited: SambaNova SN40L: Unleashing Agentic AI with Dataflow
problem: AI inference clouds must efficiently support diverse models for interactive agentic workloads (LLM assistants, chatbots, agents) while maintaining high token generation performance during memory-bound decode phase and supporting rapid model switching at scale.
method: SambaNova SN40L Reconfigurable Dataflow Unit (RDU) combines dataflow with three-tier memory (SRAM, HBM, DDR). Dataflow enables aggressive compute-graph fusion into single kernels for peak token generation; memory hierarchy reduces hardware footprint to host trillions of parameters.

title: CognitiveArm: Enabling Real-Time EEG-Controlled Prosthetic Arm Using Embodied Machine Learning
problem: Real-time EEG processing for brain-controlled prosthetics requires efficient on-device inference (filtering, feature extraction, classification) while maintaining low latency and high accuracy on resource-constrained edge hardware.
method: CognitiveArm system integrates BrainFlow EEG library with optimized deep learning models. Uses evolutionary search for Pareto-optimal DL configs via hyperparameter tuning, optimizer analysis, window selection, and ensemble combinations. Model compression (pruning/quantization) optimizes for embedded deployment. Voice commands enable mode switching.

title: Vela: A Virtualized LLM Training System with GPU Direct RoCE
problem: LLM training at scale typically requires dedicated bare-metal GPU clusters with specialized interconnects (InfiniBand, NVLink), but deploying LLM training on cloud-native virtualized infrastructure using commodity hardware and standard Ethernet-based RDMA (RoCE) introduces performance challenges from virtualization overhead and suboptimal network stack interactions.
method: Vela uses Linux KVM-based virtualization with SRIOV-based network interfaces to enable GPU-to-GPU peer-to-peer DMA (GPU Direct) across VMs without passing through the host CPU. VMs are connected via a virtualized RoCE (RDMA over Converged Ethernet) network built from off-the-shelf NICs. The system was deployed on NVIDIA A100 GPUs in IBM Cloud, using model parallelism for a 50B-parameter decoder model at ~1500 GPU scale, and insights from 2.5 years of production operation guide architectural recommendations.
